$comment: The block form of interpolate, judged by both editors alike: a template that opens with + is a value interpolate takes where it stands, judged as the value of a %s there is (unsafe-interpolation where interpolate refuses it); any other template Kotlin fills in before interpolate sees the markup (interpolate-template), with the fix that marks it. The format is the one of kotlin.json.

cases.name: a widget's root, each value marked where it stands
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Html import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate class WidgetContext(val rootId: String, val contentId: String, val eventsId: String) fun rootHtml(k: WidgetContext, customCss: String? = null, bodyHtml: Html): Html = interpolate { $$"""
$${+bodyHtml}
""".trimIndent() }

cases.name: a marked String where interpolate refuses one
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Html import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(name: String) = interpolate { """

""" }

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: name lands in data-text, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, and only a number or a boolean is let in there. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label.
interpolate always throws here: name lands in style, which is read as CSS, and only a number is let in there. Pass a number and write the unit in the markup, or choose between classes.

interpolate always throws here: name lands in onclick, which the browser runs, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Put the value in a data-* attribute and read it from there; wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

interpolate always throws here: name lands in a script, which the browser runs, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Put the value in a data-* attribute and read it from there; wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a marked URL that loads code, and one a Trusted vouches for
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Html
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate

fun f(src: String) = interpolate { """<script src="${+src}"></script><script src="${+Trusted(src)}"></script>""" }

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: src lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a String written without the mark
cases.source:

${title}

""" }

issues.message: Kotlin fills in $title before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. Mark it with +, and interpolate escapes it.

cases.name: a block of somebody else's interpolate is a string like any other
cases.source:
import com.acme.interpolate fun f(name: String) = interpolate { """

${+name}

""" }

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${+name} into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, escape it before it goes in, or build this part with kotlinx.html, which escapes text; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a template that only looks marked: an increment
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Html import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(n: Int) = interpolate { var i = n; """

${++i}

""" }

issues.message: Kotlin fills in ${++i} before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. Mark it with +, and interpolate escapes it.
